new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File (Google Books search-inside JSON, vol. id kPSdWTGZADwC = Capo 1991 A Comparative Phonology of Gbe) contains exactly one result, page_number 19, snippet_text '.. tone language, our discussion of segments is preceded by brief notes on tones ( §2.1). 2.1 Notes on tones Whatever the definition of tone language adopted ( see, for example, McCawley 1978), Gbe is, without doubt, a tone language..' -- the reported quote is there verbatim (modulo the snippet's spacing around punctuation). pp. 19-20: 'pitch phonemes', pitch-range comparisons across lects) and the sibling 'stress' 2 hits: p. 22 English loans 'stressed final syllable carry a falling tone.. tea, doctor, key, cocoa, school'; p. 206…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Capo treats all Gbe lects (Xwla/Phla included among the Phla-Phera cluster) as tone languages; search-inside finds no statement on word stress or accent anywhere in the book except that English loanwords with a stressed final syllable are borrowed with a falling tone (p. 22). No source seen states a stress position for Xwla.
new_statements.exceptions: p. 22 (snippet): English loans whose stressed final syllable carries a falling tone (tea, doctor, key, cocoa, school) -- about source-language stress, not Gbe stress.
new_statements.domain_note: Family-level comparative statement about Gbe as a whole, seen only as a snippet; not specific to Eastern Xwla and not a word-stress rule. Full sec. 2.1 not read.
new_statements.identity_note: Eastern Xwla Gbe (gbx, east2390; Seme-Kpodji / east of Lake Nokoue) vs Western Xwla Gbe (xwl, west2456; Grand-Popo). Henson & Kluge 2011 sec. 6.1: speakers recognise no dialects but the word lists and speakers distinguish an eastern and a western variety with 'accent', tone and vocabulary differences. Every Xwla-specific description on record (Hounzangbe 2020a/b, Amoni 1991, PHOIBLE 1280) concerns Western Xwla (west2456) or Grand-Popo/Houlenou varieties; Capo 1991 treats 'Phla' (Xwla) as one lect within Phla-Phera and its tone-language statement is about Gbe as a whole. Nothing specific to Eastern Xwla phonology was found.
